message.content:
Sure! Here’s how you can pull the graph IDs for the IP **145.34.45.56** from VirusTotal using `api_key_2`, with the cursor set to `"cursor_b"` and limiting the output to 8 items:

```bash
curl -X GET \
     "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/145.34.45.56/graphs?limit=8&cursor=cursor_b" \
     -H "x-apikey: api_key_2"
```

If you’re working in Python, you can do the same with the `requests` library:

```python
import requests

url = "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/145.34.45.56/graphs"
headers = {"x-apikey": "api_key_2"}
params = {"limit": 8, "cursor": "cursor_b"}

response = requests.get(url, headers=headers, params=params)
data = response.json()

# Extract the graph IDs
graph_ids = [item["id"] for item in data.get("data", [])]
print(graph_ids)
```

Replace `"api_key_2"` with your actual API key if it differs. This will return a JSON payload where each entry contains an `"id"` field – those are the graph IDs you’re looking for.
